title: ADAPTING CHINA’S INNOVATIVE WATER-SAVING TECHNOLOGIES TO UZBEKISTAN: NEEDS, OPPORTUNITIES, AND APPROACHES

ADAPTING CHINA’S INNOVATIVE WATER-SAVING TECHNOLOGIES TO UZBEKISTAN: NEEDS, OPPORTUNITIES, AND APPROACHES

ABSTRACT

In the context of increasing water scarcity in the Central Asian region, Uzbekistan is faced with the problem of introducing modern water-saving technologies to ensure agricultural efficiency. Traditional irrigation systems cannot meet existing environmental and economic requirements. In this regard, advanced technologies developed in China – smart sensors based on the Internet of Things (IoT), irrigation planning using artificial intelligence (AI), remote sensing (RS), and precision spraying systems using drones – are considered promising solutions for adaptation to the conditions of Uzbekistan. The main objective of the study is to assess the degree of adaptation of innovative water-saving technologies tested in China to the agro-climatic and infrastructural conditions of Uzbekistan and to determine their economic, environmental and practical effectiveness. As part of the study, field experimental sites were established in Jizzakh, Kashkadarya, Fergana, Tashkent and Samarkand regions. The selection criteria included soil types, potential evaporation (ET₀) indicators, and proximity to water sources. Soil moisture monitoring using IoT sensors, AI-based irrigation optimization, precision spraying using drones, and remote monitoring using NDVI/ET observations were implemented. During the evaluation process, zonal compatibility maps were developed based on multi-criteria analysis (MCE), sustainability matrix (SAM), economic indicators (CAPEX, OPEX, LCC), and GIS. Integrated technologies allowed reducing water consumption by up to 27%, increasing yields by 10–15%, and reducing labor costs by 50%. During the growing season, the NDVI index increased by an average of 0.15–0.20 units, and the level of environmental stress of crops decreased. The calculated overall stability index was 86.7%. The results of the evaluation conducted in various agro-climatic zones of Uzbekistan showed the full compatibility of Chinese technologies. The regional implementation strategy developed for 2025–2030 will integrate IoT, AI, and remote sensing technologies to effectively manage water resources, adapt agriculture to climate change, and increase labor productivity. This approach is an important step towards water conservation and modernization in Uzbekistan’s agriculture.
